## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

---
name: reference-review-harness-claude-needs-foreground
description: "REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review fails with a bare \"Execution error\" as a background task, so run it in the foreground — but as of 2026-08-02 claude is Fable-5 quota-blocked and CODEX is the working reviewer, the reverse of what this note used to say"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 82368b87-6555-4432-bce4-6459714348f7
  modified: 2026-08-05T11:47:44.034Z
---

`REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review` **must run in the foreground**. Launched as a
background task it dies at the `>> invoking claude review` line, and the
preserved inline output is exactly 15 bytes: `Execution error`. Three
consecutive attempts on PR #2399 failed identically; the same command run
synchronously in the foreground succeeded immediately (verdict 92/88).

The failure is silent-ish and looks like an external kill, so it invites
re-running the same thing. Check
`/tmp/lobu-review-claude-inline.*` — a 15-byte `Execution error` file is the
signature.

## REVERSED 2026-08-02: claude is the blocked one, codex works

This note used to say codex was quota-blocked until Aug 5 and foreground claude was
the only path. That flipped. On PR #2437:

- `REVIEWER_CLI=claude` fails **immediately**, both for `make review-fix` and
  `make review`, with `You've reached your Fable 5 limit.` The claude reviewer is
  backed by Fable 5, so a Fable quota exhausts it. `make review` **fails closed** and
  explicitly refuses to fall back: "The review gate fails closed and will not fall
  back to another reviewer."
- `REVIEWER_CLI=codex` runs fine — it just takes **longer than 600s**, so a
  foreground Bash call times out and gets backgrounded. Codex tolerates background
  execution (only claude has the `Execution error` problem), so backgrounding it is
  correct, not a workaround.

**Do not trust a recorded reviewer-availability window.** Both reviewers are quota-
gated on separate budgets that move independently; the only way to know which works
is to try one.

## FLIPPED BACK 2026-08-05: codex blocked, foreground claude works

On PR #2499, `make review` (default `auto` → codex) failed with
`ERROR: You've hit your usage limit. ... try again at Aug 10th, 2026 1:53 AM`
and `make: *** [review] Error 1`. `REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review` **in the
foreground** then succeeded on the first try (verdict bug_free 80, 0 blockers)
and posted the `pi-review` status normally.

So within three days the working reviewer flipped codex→claude→codex→claude. The
foreground rule for claude still holds. Budget ~20 min of foreground wall-clock.

`scripts/review.sh` supports only `codex|claude`.

Related: [[reference_review_harness_quota_and_schema_traps]],
[[project_review_harness_codex_single_point]], [[feedback_run_review_without_asking]]

---
name: reference_worktree_remove_fails_with_submodules
description: git worktree remove refuses on every lobu worktree (owletto submodule) — use rm -rf + git worktree prune; budget ~20s each because of node_modules
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dc1df443-8162-4cd9-b062-3e67f86994ab
  modified: 2026-07-30T04:30:49.535Z
---

`git worktree remove .claude/worktrees/<name>` fails on **every** lobu worktree with:

```
fatal: working trees containing submodules cannot be moved or removed
```

That is the `owletto` submodule, which `make task-setup` pins into each worktree — so it
is not an occasional case, it is all of them.

Working removal:

```sh
rm -rf ".claude/worktrees/<name>" && git worktree prune
```

`git worktree prune` (from the main checkout) reaps the stale metadata afterwards. This
does NOT delete the branch ref — commits stay reachable via `refs/heads/<branch>`, which
is what makes a bulk sweep low-risk even if one entry is misclassified.

**Budget the time.** Each worktree carries a populated `node_modules`, so `rm -rf` runs
~15–25s. A 31-worktree sweep exceeded a 10-minute foreground timeout at 22 removed —
run bulk cleanup in the background.

## Picking what is safe to remove

Do NOT classify by ancestry. `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` reports `1` for
almost every squash-merged branch, because a squash writes a new commit with no ancestry
link (see [[reference_squash_merge_breaks_ancestry_checks]]). On a 67-worktree sweep that
misread 29 merged branches as unmerged.

Classify against real PR state instead:

```sh
gh pr list --state merged --limit 400 --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName' > /tmp/merged.txt
gh pr list --state open   --limit 200 --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName' > /tmp/open.txt
```

Remove only when the tree is clean AND the branch is in the merged list. Re-check
`git status --porcelain` immediately before each `rm -rf` rather than trusting an earlier
snapshot — worktrees go dirty on their own from build artifacts (`pi-loader-hardening`
did exactly that mid-sweep and was correctly skipped).

Both PRs **MERGED 2026-08-05**. Only prod-verification remains.

## 1. lobu#2509 — feat(server): surface a retained tool request from the activity UI
Squash commit **`1d6a1b1cb3da0ee52a4ced8c3fe786b7b6ba376c`**.

- Net diff was only **2 files, +16/−5**: `request_status` (a retention *outcome* enum —
  `complete`/`too_large`/`unavailable`, never call content) stops being stripped on list
  reads, so a card can show the peek affordance. `request` and `request_bytes` stay
  author/admin-gated, test-asserted for a non-author member.
- The rest of the feature shipped through other doors: retention mechanic in #2505, the
  UI half in owletto#723 which reached main via #2511's already-approved pin. Head
  `7eba994f` pinned `400bcb14` = main's pin → **zero pointer delta**, so `ui-review`
  passed as "not applicable" and owletto#723's `/ui-approve` was never needed.
- Final `pi-review` on the settled head: bug_free 92, simplicity 95, slop 0, 0 bugs,
  0 blockers, risk low.

## 2. lobu#2513 — fix(server): report device liveness truthfully instead of a 20-minute guess
Squash commit **`dc76334b9d875e90f1130562bf9699f665d35f8f`**.

- `check-drift` was red **only** from the repo-wide owletto pin gap (branch pinned
  `2741388c`, owletto/main at `400bcb14`). Merging `origin/main` after #2509 landed
  carried the pin forward and cleared it — no bump PR was needed, confirming
  [[reference_worktree_stale_submodule_pin_fails_check_drift]].
- `ui-review` is a REQUIRED check that had **never reported** on this PR — that alone
  held `mergeStateStatus` at `BLOCKED` after every other gate was green. Running
  `make ui-review` (passes as not applicable) was the missing step, not a retry.
- Final `pi-review`: bug_free 90, simplicity 88, slop 5, 0 bugs, 0 blockers, risk medium.

## The reviewer-quota cascade that blocked this for hours

Every reviewer was exhausted simultaneously: codex CLI out until **Aug 10**, all three
ChatGPT slots dead, grok/zai/qwen each failed on real workload (a 2-token probe does NOT
detect exhaustion — all three answered a probe and then died mid-review). `pi-review` is
a required status with `enforce_admins`, so **`--admin` cannot bypass it** — GitHub
rejects the merge. There was no path but to wait for a quota window.

`REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review` **in the foreground** worked on the first try once the
session limit reset at **16:40 London**, on both PRs. See
[[reference_review_harness_claude_needs_foreground]].

## Prod-verify owed after rollout (gate on the SQUASH commit, merge-commit-first order)

1. **#2505** (`0a401094`) — new `manage_operations` audit rows record
   `{"action":"list_available",…}` instead of two sentinels (`events` where
   `origin_type='tool_invocation'`, check `payload_data->>'args_preview_redacted'`).
2. **#2509** (`1d6a1b1c`) — an Activity audit row is clickable and its peek shows the
   request body: `/{org}/activity?peek=1&peek_content_ids=<event_id>`. Also confirm a
   **non-author** sees neither `request` nor `request_bytes`.
3. **#2513** (`dc76334b`) — a device silent >2 min reports `device_offline` with age in
   the reason. Real risk: **false-offline flapping** — a >2-min server-side
   poll-ingestion stall would read the whole fleet offline, which the old 20-minute
   window absorbed. A burst across unrelated devices means the ingest stalled, not the
   devices.

## Environment notes

- Worktrees `audit-request-peek`, `device-liveness-window`, `audit-enum-args` are all
  removed and their branches deleted.
- **`lobu_test` DB is inconsistent** — concurrent vitest runs from two worktrees left it
  missing tables. Use a per-branch DB or create a fresh one and let the harness migrate.

[[reference_squash_merge_breaks_ancestry_checks]],
[[reference_check_drift_is_gated_by_ui_approve]],

All done. Here's what those five files were.

**Two were unrelated cruft — reverted:**

`.claude/settings.json` dropped an empty `"PostToolUse": []` and added an empty `permissions {allow:[], deny:[]}`. Both no-ops, pure churn in a checked-in shared file. `.gitignore` added 8 lines for **IronBee** — a tool with zero footprint in this repo (no `.ironbee` dir, and the only reference anywhere was the gitignore line itself) — plus a `.claude/settings.local.json` entry already covered by `**/.claude/settings.local.json` on line 4.

**Three were one coherent change — a Qwen/DashScope provider** added during the reviewer-quota hunt. It had two genuine bugs:

The serious one was in `model-resolver.ts`: `qwen: "DASHSCOPE_API_KEY"` was placed inside `DEFAULT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL_ENV`, a map of provider → *base URL* env var. `session-runner.ts:842` does `providerBaseUrl = credentialStore.get(baseUrlEnvVar)`, so a Qwen run would have used **the API key string as its base URL** — a failed request with the secret embedded in a malformed URL, landing in error text and logs. The canonical derivation at `base-provider-module.ts:250` is `credentialEnvVarName.replace("_KEY", "_BASE_URL")`, so the correct value is `DASHSCOPE_API_BASE_URL`.

The second was collateral damage: `config/providers.json` flipped the **OpenCode Zen** provider's `defaultModel` from `claude-sonnet-4-6` to a fabricated `qwen-2.5-coder-32b-instruct` — note the dot, which isn't even DashScope's real id format. Wrong provider entirely.

I fixed both, plus a consistency gap (Qwen was the only key-based provider whose `apiKeyInstructions` was dead plain text rather than a link — 16 of 18 use an anchor). Resolver tests pass 34/34 and the JSON parses.

Answering #1 first, because it changes the shape of the PR:

**Yes — and it should be *purely* config.** I traced the runtime path: for any provider in `config/providers.json`, `api-key-provider-module.ts:132` derives `baseUrlEnvVar` as `envVarName.replace("_KEY","_BASE_URL")` → `DASHSCOPE_API_BASE_URL`, and `registerDynamicProvider()` writes that into the map at runtime. So the `model-resolver.ts` line isn't just wrong, it's **unnecessary** — and actively harmful, since `registerDynamicProvider` has an `if (!alreadyRegistered)` guard, so a hardcoded entry *wins* over the config-derived one and can silently drift from `providers.json`. Dropping it makes this 2 files, zero TypeScript.

The runtime already derives everything else from `envVarName`:

A hardcoded `DEFAULT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL_ENV` entry would **shadow** that derivation — `registerDynamicProvider` skips registration when the id is already present — so the hardcoded value could silently drift from `providers.json`. That map is documented as a fallback for providers *absent* from the config, so this change deliberately adds **zero TypeScript**.

The added field set is a strict subset of an existing sibling provider's (`groq`), minus `stt`.

- `providers-live.yml` skips the Qwen row until a `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` repo secret exists, so scheduled live-provider CI is unaffected

Low. Additive config for a provider nobody is connected to yet; no existing provider row is touched.

---
name: feedback_post_merge_prod_verify_wakeup
description: "After merging a prod-visible PR, set a self-rescheduling ScheduleWakeup carrying the rollout gate and write the result back to memory — the pattern already works, it was just written down nowhere"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: f788a6c1-21e9-429d-a821-45098b92a603
  modified: 2026-07-29T19:06:59.473Z
---

Four programs sit on an "OWED prod verify" line with no closure entry:
[[project_mcp_client_activity_surface]] (marked COMPLETE 2026-07-28),
[[project_prod_mcp_reliability_sweep]] (PRs #1980–#1985, 2026-07-15),
[[project_approval_live_state_interaction_contract]], and multi-replica interaction-card loss.

**The diagnosis to reject:** it is NOT that the 30–60 min Flux rollout ([[project_prod_flux_image_automation]])
outlives the session. That was already solved — on 2026-07-14 a session used a self-rescheduling
`ScheduleWakeup` that polled `kubectl exec … grep '^APP_GIT_SHA='` plus
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha>`, ran the live check the moment the rollout landed, and edited memory
to "FULLY E2E-VERIFIED on prod". `ScheduleWakeup` appears in 19 sessions but almost entirely for CI/PR
polling. **The working pattern exists and is applied inconsistently because it was written down nowhere.**

**How to apply** — when a merged PR touches a prod-visible surface, before ending the turn:
1. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) whose prompt carries BOTH the rollout gate (deployed
   SHA → `git merge-base --is-ancestor`) and the specific checks from the PR body.
2. On landing, run the live check, then write the verdict back into the program's memory file as a
   closure line. A program with no closure line is unverified, regardless of what its status says.

**Do NOT build a `prod-verify` GitHub issue queue or a cron agent for this.** Memory already carries
closures fine elsewhere ([[project_slack_workspace_fencing_prs]], [[project_conversation_tools_pr]],
[[project_sidebar_nav_runtime_cred_fields]]); the gap is the habit, not the infrastructure.

Note AGENTS.md gates e2e PRE-merge but said nothing about post-deploy until this was added to
"Ship a change". Distinct from [[feedback-e2e-verification-required]], which covers the pre-merge side.
Exclude human-blocked items (e.g. Slack Grid needs the user to install) — those are not context-loss.

**FIRST REAL USE — WORKS, 2026-07-29 (closure).** Ran the step-10 gate end-to-end on both PRs merged
that day. Against `APP_GIT_SHA=87650cee2`, the gate correctly returned *deployed* for #2283 and *not
yet* for #2282 — the exact distinction the pre-fix branch-head version could never make (see
[[reference_squash_merge_breaks_ancestry_checks]]). A `Monitor` polling `kubectl exec … APP_GIT_SHA`
every 120s caught #2282's rollout ~30 min later at `bff73e8a4`, and re-verification after that second
rollout still showed 11/11 correct tiers, fresh pods `1/1 Running` / 0 restarts, and no new error class.
**A SINGLE `/health` PROBE IS AN UNSOUND ROLLOUT GATE (learned the hard way 2026-07-29, #2325).** `curl https://app.lobu.ai/health | .revision` hits ONE pod chosen by the load balancer. During a rolling deploy `summaries-app-lobu-app` runs old and new ReplicaSets side by side — all Ready, all serving — so consecutive probes returned `7c27a1377f` then `8c9706632`, and the gate fired on the first new pod while a #2322 pod was still taking traffic. It reports "any replica is new", never "all replicas are new". Two separate monitors built on it both false-positived.

**Gate on Kubernetes state instead**, which is the actual rollout fact:
```
kubectl get pods -n summaries-prod -l app.kubernetes.io/component=api \
  -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.containers[0].image}{"\n"}{end}' | grep -cv '<new-image-tag>'
```
Wait for `0`. Note `kubectl get deploy` is ALSO misleading — it showed `2/2 READY, 2 UP-TO-DATE` while a third pod from the previous ReplicaSet was still Running and Ready; only the per-pod image listing exposed it. Image tags are `ghcr.io/lobu-ai/lobu-app:YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<build>` and the timestamp is the build minute, so it is easy to map a tag to a merge.

**Why it is not merely cosmetic:** healing a durable row on a new pod and then landing the follow-up call on an old pod means the old code re-evaluates state it has no concept of. For #2325 the refreshed proposal is stamped `version: 2`; version-unaware code compares the hash directly, mismatches, and bounces the run back to pending — indistinguishable from the fix not working. Wait for the rollout to finish before touching prod rows.

**Practical notes for next time:** the prod container has **no python3** — copy the bundle out
(`kubectl exec … cat > local`) and parse locally rather than in-pod; `grep -o` truncates on the minified
4.5 MB bundle, so pull once and search the file (same lesson as
[[feedback_compact_pr_status_and_ci_logs]]). Always attribute residual errors before declaring green:
21x `[device-connectors] Failed to wire device connector` looked alarming but originates in
`worker-api/device-reconcile.ts`, untouched by either PR and pre-existing.

`.codex/visualizations/` (116 KB, 3 files, Aug 1) — standalone HTML visualizations Codex wrote during the social-interest radar work ("Social Interest Radar Flow", "…Example Lab").

Neither belongs in git. Setting up the ignore as its own PR since it's a separate concern from the provider config.

## PROD-VERIFIED 2026-08-05 (closure) — deployed SHA `9224fce77`, both pods `20260805-161803`, 0 restarts

**#2513 verified with a live transition capture, and it discriminates correctly.** Sampling
`connections.list` twice 30s apart across 18 device connections / 4 physical devices:
three devices advanced `device_last_seen_at` by 28–30s (healthy ~30s poll cadence = **4x
headroom** under the new 120s window), while "Burak's MacBook Pro" advanced by **0s** and
flipped `device_online: true` @98s → `false` @128s, `device_status: "offline"`.

That is the exact discrimination the feared failure mode needs: a server-side ingest stall
would have taken **all four** devices offline together. One device going silent while the
other three keep polling on schedule = genuinely offline, truthfully reported. Under the old
20-minute window that same machine would have read "online" for ~18 more minutes.

**#2509 verified on the read path.** `knowledge.read` with a single content_id AND with three
content_ids (the list shape) both return `request_status: "complete"` — the strip is gone,
which is the whole change. The exact-id read also serves `request`.

**Not verified, stated plainly:** (a) the non-author gating on `request`/`request_bytes` — this
session authenticates as the workspace owner/admin, so it cannot observe the denied case; it
rests on the integration test that asserts a non-author gets neither. (b) #2513's timeout
*reason string* naming the age — no run dispatched to the offline device in the recent 40
failed runs, so that text was never produced in prod. Forcing it would need a prod write.

Both PRs **MERGED 2026-08-05**. Only prod-verification remains.

## 1. lobu#2509 — feat(server): surface a retained tool request from the activity UI
Squash commit **`1d6a1b1cb3da0ee52a4ced8c3fe786b7b6ba376c`**.

- Net diff was only **2 files, +16/−5**: `request_status` (a retention *outcome* enum —
  `complete`/`too_large`/`unavailable`, never call content) stops being stripped on list
  reads, so a card can show the peek affordance. `request` and `request_bytes` stay
  author/admin-gated, test-asserted for a non-author member.
- The rest of the feature shipped through other doors: retention mechanic in #2505, the
  UI half in owletto#723 which reached main via #2511's already-approved pin. Head
  `7eba994f` pinned `400bcb14` = main's pin → **zero pointer delta**, so `ui-review`
  passed as "not applicable" and owletto#723's `/ui-approve` was never needed.
- Final `pi-review` on the settled head: bug_free 92, simplicity 95, slop 0, 0 bugs,
  0 blockers, risk low.

## 2. lobu#2513 — fix(server): report device liveness truthfully instead of a 20-minute guess
Squash commit **`dc76334b9d875e90f1130562bf9699f665d35f8f`**.

- `check-drift` was red **only** from the repo-wide owletto pin gap (branch pinned
  `2741388c`, owletto/main at `400bcb14`). Merging `origin/main` after #2509 landed
  carried the pin forward and cleared it — no bump PR was needed, confirming
  [[reference_worktree_stale_submodule_pin_fails_check_drift]].
- `ui-review` is a REQUIRED check that had **never reported** on this PR — that alone
  held `mergeStateStatus` at `BLOCKED` after every other gate was green. Running
  `make ui-review` (passes as not applicable) was the missing step, not a retry.
- Final `pi-review`: bug_free 90, simplicity 88, slop 5, 0 bugs, 0 blockers, risk medium.

## The reviewer-quota cascade that blocked this for hours

Every reviewer was exhausted simultaneously: codex CLI out until **Aug 10**, all three
ChatGPT slots dead, grok/zai/qwen each failed on real workload (a 2-token probe does NOT
detect exhaustion — all three answered a probe and then died mid-review). `pi-review` is
a required status with `enforce_admins`, so **`--admin` cannot bypass it** — GitHub
rejects the merge. There was no path but to wait for a quota window.

`REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review` **in the foreground** worked on the first try once the
session limit reset at **16:40 London**, on both PRs. See
[[reference_review_harness_claude_needs_foreground]].

## Prod-verify owed after rollout (gate on the SQUASH commit, merge-commit-first order)

1. **#2505** (`0a401094`) — new `manage_operations` audit rows record
   `{"action":"list_available",…}` instead of two sentinels (`events` where
   `origin_type='tool_invocation'`, check `payload_data->>'args_preview_redacted'`).
2. **#2509** (`1d6a1b1c`) — an Activity audit row is clickable and its peek shows the
   request body: `/{org}/activity?peek=1&peek_content_ids=<event_id>`. Also confirm a
   **non-author** sees neither `request` nor `request_bytes`.
3. **#2513** (`dc76334b`) — a device silent >2 min reports `device_offline` with age in
   the reason. Real risk: **false-offline flapping** — a >2-min server-side
   poll-ingestion stall would read the whole fleet offline, which the old 20-minute
   window absorbed. A burst across unrelated devices means the ingest stalled, not the
   devices.

## Environment notes

- Worktrees `audit-request-peek`, `device-liveness-window`, `audit-enum-args` are all
  removed and their branches deleted.
- **`lobu_test` DB is inconsistent** — concurrent vitest runs from two worktrees left it
  missing tables. Use a per-branch DB or create a fresh one and let the harness migrate.

name: project_qwen_provider_uncommitted_experiment
description: "Qwen/DashScope provider SHIPPED as lobu#2522 (config-only); the API-key-as-base-URL bug it carried, and the providers.json group-name contract that only CI catches"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  modified: 2026-08-05T17:00:00.000Z
---

**SHIPPED 2026-08-05 as lobu#2522, squash `848dfcb0ebb0d709df57895768edd9d38c9a3b20`** —
config-only, 2 files (+27). Originated as an uncommitted experiment in the **main checkout**
during the reviewer-quota cascade (see [[project_audit_peek_and_liveness_merge_handoff]]).

## A provider addition should be CONFIG-ONLY — the TS entry is a trap

The experiment put `qwen: "DASHSCOPE_API_KEY"` into **`DEFAULT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL_ENV`**
(`agent-worker/src/runtime/model-resolver.ts`), a provider → **base URL** env map.
`session-runner.ts:842` does `providerBaseUrl = credentialStore.get(baseUrlEnvVar)`, so a
Qwen run would have used **the API key string as its base URL** — the secret embedded in a
malformed URL surfacing in errors and logs.

It was also **unnecessary**: `api-key-provider-module.ts:132` already derives
`baseUrlEnvVar` as `envVarName.replace("_KEY", "_BASE_URL")` → `DASHSCOPE_API_BASE_URL`, and
`registerDynamicProvider()` (`session-runner.ts:797`) installs it at startup. Worse, that
function early-returns on `if (!alreadyRegistered)`, so **a hardcoded entry WINS over the
config-derived one** and can silently drift from `providers.json`. The map is documented as a
fallback for providers *absent* from the config. Adding a provider needs **zero TypeScript**.

## The group-name contract, which only integration CI catches

`config/providers.json` group `name` must equal what `url-builder.ts:222 providerDisplayName()`
derives: `PROVIDER_DISPLAY_NAMES[slug]` if pinned, else **capitalise the slug**. The contract
test is `packages/server/src/utils/__tests__/render-agent-error.test.ts` → "matches
config/providers.json for every registered provider", and it runs in the
**integration-vitest** shard — so `pre-commit` (biome + tsc), `make review`, and every fast
gate pass while it fails. Naming the group `"Qwen / DashScope"` against slug `qwen` failed
with `expected 'Qwen returned an error:' to be 'Qwen / DashScope returned an error:'`.

Fix was to name the group `"Qwen"` — every sibling group uses a single product name
(`Groq`, `z.ai`, `OpenCode Zen`), and the vendor detail belongs in `description` /
`apiKeyInstructions`. Adding a `PROVIDER_DISPLAY_NAMES` override would have been the wrong
lever for a name that derives fine.

**`make review` did NOT catch this** (verdict 88, 0 bugs) — it ran a couple of bun tests, not
the vitest shard. A config change can still break a contract test; wait for CI.

Also fixed en route: the experiment had flipped the unrelated **OpenCode Zen** group's
`defaultModel` from `claude-sonnet-4-6` to a fabricated `qwen-2.5-coder-32b-instruct`.

## Follow-ups

- Not yet prod-verified: Qwen appearing in the provider-connect UI (merged after the
  `9224fce77` rollout). Gate on `848dfcb0e`.
- `providers-live.yml` skips the Qwen row until a `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` repo secret exists —
  see [[project_providers_live_ci]].
- `.pi-subagents/` and `.codex/` were gitignored separately in **#2523** (`a6b9cd015`).

Related: [[reference_org_provider_needs_base_url]], [[project_agent_model_provider_resolution]]

content.text:
All four items are done, and prod verification is armed for the one piece still rolling out.

**1. Qwen provider — shipped as #2522** (`848dfcb0e`). You were right that it's a config change, and it turned out to be *more* config-only than the original: I dropped the `model-resolver.ts` line entirely rather than fixing it, because `api-key-provider-module.ts:132` already derives `DASHSCOPE_API_BASE_URL` from `envVarName`, and `registerDynamicProvider` early-returns on `if (!alreadyRegistered)` — so a hardcoded entry would have *won* over the config and could silently drift. Final diff: 2 files, +27, zero TypeScript.

CI caught a real bug my review missed. There's a contract test asserting every `providers.json` group name equals what `providerDisplayName()` derives (capitalised slug unless pinned). `Qwen / DashScope` vs slug `qwen` failed with `expected 'Qwen returned an error:' to be 'Qwen / DashScope returned an error:'`. I renamed the group to `Qwen` — the right fix regardless, since every sibling uses a single product name and the vendor detail already sits in `description`. Worth knowing: **that test lives in the `integration-vitest` shard**, so pre-commit, `tsc`, and `make review` (verdict 88, "0 bugs") all passed while it was broken.

On merging without review — I couldn't. `pi-review` and `ui-review` are required statuses with `enforce_admins`; GitHub rejected the merge outright. I did skip `pre-pr` and `review-fix`.

**2. Prod verification — #2509 and #2513 are verified.** The rollout had already advanced to `9224fce77` (both pods on one image, 0 restarts).

For #2513 I caught the transition live. Sampling 18 device connections twice, 30s apart: three devices advanced `last_seen` by 28–30s, while the MacBook Pro advanced by **0s** and flipped `online: true` @98s → `false` @128s, `device_status: "offline"`. That's the discrimination that matters — an ingest stall would have taken all four devices offline together; one going silent while three keep polling is genuinely offline, truthfully reported. Under the old 20-minute window that machine would have read "online" for ~18 more minutes. Healthy devices poll every ~30s, so 4x headroom under the 120s window — no flapping risk.

For #2509, `knowledge.read` with one content_id *and* with three (the list shape) both return `request_status: "complete"`. The strip is gone, which is the entire change.

Two things I did **not** verify, to be straight about it: the non-author gating on `request`/`request_bytes` — I'm authenticated as workspace owner, so I can't observe the denied case; it rests on the integration test. And #2513's timeout *reason string* naming the age — no run dispatched to the offline device, so that text was never produced in prod, and forcing it would mean a prod write.

**3. The directories** — `.pi-subagents/` (1.3 MB) is pi subagent transcripts and prompts; `.codex/` (116 KB) is Codex-generated HTML visualizations from the social-interest radar work. Both gitignored in **#2523** (`a6b9cd015`), as a separate PR since it's a distinct concern. They still show untracked in your main checkout only because it sits on `feat/behavior-executors`, which predates that merge.

**4.** #2522 hasn't rolled out yet (merged minutes ago). A self-rescheduling wakeup is set for ~25 min carrying the gate — pod-image check rather than a `/health` probe, ancestry test in merge-commit-first order — plus a regression check that OpenCode Zen's `defaultModel` is still `claude-sonnet-4-6`. It writes its own closure line to memory and stops.

Confidence:
- **#2513 prod behavior — 97%.** Observed the actual online→offline transition with a control group of three devices still polling. Only the reason-string wording is unverified.
- **#2509 prod behavior — 88%.** Verified the server contract on both read shapes; the non-author denial is inferred from tests, not observed, and I didn't load the Activity UI.
- **#2522 correctness — 92%.** Full CI green including the shard that caught the bug, plus the contract test run locally 13/13. Not 100% until it's live in the catalog.
- **#2523 — 99%.** Ignore-only; verified zero tracked files match either pattern.

Worth your attention: `git worktree prune` would not reap the qwen worktree even with `--expire now` (the `modules/` submodule metadata blocks it) — I had to `rm -rf .git/worktrees/<name>`. That's a sharper version of the workaround already in your notes, and it'll bite any future cleanup sweep.
